title: SECTION E — ERECTION, EJACULATION & PHYSIOLOGICAL RESPONSES

questions.prompt: A client loses his erection halfway through Lunez. What should the therapist do?

Assume the massage has failed.
Remain calm, professional, and neutral, and continue the approved massage.
End the session immediately in embarrassment.

options: Erection is a possible physiological response, not an instruction and not the measure of success or failure.
No erection always means the therapist is unskilled.
A strong erection means the therapist should become personally involved.
Erection means the client now owns the therapist’s time.

Stop. Consent can be withdrawn. Pause, clarify, and do not assume.

options: Payment buys the approved Lunez service only. It does not buy the therapist’s body, sexual access, or permission to ignore boundaries.
Payment means the client can request anything.
Payment removes the need for consent.
Payment transfers the therapist’s personal number to the client.

title: SECTION H — HYGIENE, SAFETY & HEALTH CONCERNS

questions.prompt: During preparation for Lunez, the therapist notices an open sore in an area that would normally be massaged. What should the therapist do?
options: Massage around it firmly so it heals faster.
Cover it with extra oil and continue.
Stop, do not massage through it, and escalate or refer rather than proceed as normal.
Ask the client to wash it after the session.

questions.prompt: A client reports severe unexplained genital pain and visible swelling. How should this affect the therapist's decision to proceed with Lunez?
options: The therapist should not simply proceed. Pause, modify, stop, escalate, or advise appropriate health assessment.
Proceed with deeper pressure to reduce the swelling.
Proceed if the client insists, with no further thought.
Proceed but skip reporting.

questions.prompt: A client says, “I have painful urination and fever, but please massage deeply around my prostate area.” What should the therapist do?
options: Do as asked because the client consented.
Do not proceed as requested. This is outside safe Lunez practice and needs stop / refer / escalate, not deep massage.
Offer internal prostate massage instead.
Give medical advice and diagnose the cause.

questions.prompt: Why are hygiene procedures particularly important during Lunez Massage?
options: Because Lunez involves intimate regions and may involve bodily fluids, so handwashing, linen, clean-up, barriers, equipment, and room reset must be strict.
Because hygiene is only for Zura Massage.
Because perfume can replace cleaning.
Because clients prefer therapists not to wash their hands.

questions.prompt: Two therapists complete Lunez. During the session, the client repeatedly asked for prohibited sexual activity. They refused but decide not to report it because “nothing eventually happened.” What is wrong with this decision?
options: Nothing. Refusal is enough.
They should have agreed to one prohibited request to keep the client.
Repeated prohibited requests are a boundary concern. Hiding it leaves leadership unaware and weakens safety and accountability.
They should have argued with the client in front of the next guest.

questions.prompt: Describe the behaviour of a therapist who demonstrates strong professional understanding while performing Lunez.
options: Structured, calm, professional, controlled, boundaried, hygienic, timed, and complete, with consent and client comfort protected.
Rushes to ejaculation and jokes about the client’s body.
Extends unofficially until release, then leaves without closing.
Allows reciprocal touching if the client is polite.

questions.prompt: After Lunez, a therapist says, “The client never became erect, so I clearly performed badly.” What factors should actually be used to assess the therapist's performance?
options: Whether ejaculation occurred, and how quickly.
Whether the Lunez standard, technique, timing, communication, boundaries, hygiene, and dignity of client and therapist were followed.
Whether the client asked for the therapist’s number.
Whether the massage hurt.
